GPT-6 Astra appears to be a massive jump in opaque reasoning ability: it looks like it can solve hard competition math problems entirely in its head (as in, without verbalized reasoning) while prior AIs could solve basic word problems.

This seems extremely concerning!

That is, if these benchmark results are representative (see the highlighted caveats in the image, I'm particularly worried about contamination).

Related to this, UK AISI found Astra has much worse monitorability.

I'd guess this jump is downstream of architectural changes (with increased serial depth) though a normal large pretrain scale up is a plausible cause. If the next few model generations involve similar jumps (presumably these jumps would be downstream of a transition to full-on opaque reasoning architectures with extreme depth), then chain-of-thought would no longer be a meaningful oversight tool.

OpenAI seems to imply (Edit: they are just noting this I think) that it's good for safety/monitoring to make reasoning=None unavailable to the public because Astra has much higher latent reasoning capabilities (with less need for CoT). But this actually makes it even more important to study AI capabilities without CoT!

Edit: I've been convinced they weren't implying this and were just trying to note this.

Not allowing people to query the AI without reasoning doesn't make these monitorability problems go away (the model can still latently reason without verbalizing it when reasoning is on, and the reasoning-on case is the more concerning one anyway given the higher capabilities)!

It's possible (Edit: I now think "likely") that OpenAI didn't mean to imply that not allowing for reasoning=None is good for monitorability. And it's pretty likely that the reason they are doing this is something more like jailbreak robustness or preventing distillation (AIs might spill reasoning into the output if they can't reason in the normal field). But it would have been good if AI companies (including OpenAI and Anthropic) more explicitly acknowledged that not allowing for disabling reasoning is actively bad for monitorability science! (Note that disabling reasoning has historically been an important way to elicit subversion capabilities for testing, in addition to being necessary for testing no-CoT capabilities.)

To be clear, I don't think it's extremely important to make reasoning=None available to the public, but I do think that getting a better understanding of the AI's no-CoT capabilities is very important given the massive apparent jump, and external researchers not being able to run experiments on this is a problem! (This isn't just an OpenAI problem; Anthropic also doesn't allow for disabling CoT for Fable.) I think some kind of researcher access program that gives more API features, including disabling reasoning, and has a relatively low bar for entry would be a good step if there are good reasons disabling reasoning can't be made publicly available.
